title: Maximum Consecutive Ones III
contract: In a binary array, flip at most k zeroes. Return the longest resulting consecutive-one window; k ≥ 0.
brute: int best=0;for(int l=0;l<a.length;l++){int zeroes=0;for(int r=l;r<a.length;r++){if(a[r]==0)zeroes++;if(zeroes>k)break;best=Math.max(best,r-l+1);emit("Test a window within the flip budget","range",new int[]{l,r},"zeroes",zeroes,"best",best);}}return best;
optimal: int l=0,zeroes=0,best=0;for(int r=0;r<a.length;r++){if(a[r]==0)zeroes++;while(zeroes>k)if(a[l++]==0)zeroes--;best=Math.max(best,r-l+1);emit("Shrink until the flip budget is respected","range",new int[]{l,r},"zeroes",zeroes,"best",best);}return best;
reasoning: For each start, count zeroes while extending until the flip budget is exceeded.
The only state needed for validity is the number of zeroes inside the current window.
Removing left elements cannot increase that count, so the window can be restored with one monotone left pointer. Do not actually mutate the input to simulate flips.
